newsitem.title: CHINA: China B shares end sharply down, A shares rebound.
newsitem.headline: China B shares end sharply down, A shares rebound.

text.p: Hard currency B shares on China's two stock exchanges ended sharply down on Tuesday, with market sentiment severely weakened by falls in the past few days and the poor debut of a newcomer, brokers said.

But domestic A shares closed up on both the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges on a technical rebound supported by market speculation that Beijing might slow new share issues in the wake of the recent losses, they said.
Shanghai's B share index ended the day down 2.841 points or 3.83 percent at 71.304 points on volume of 12.451 million shares worth $7.773 million.
In Shenzhen, the Hong Kong dollar-denominated B share index plunged 6.38 points or 5.00 percent to 121.30 points as turnover grew to HK$287.9 million from Monday's HK$50 million.
Brokers said falls in the past few days, partly due to heavy new share issues right before China's takeover of Hong Kong on July 1, greatly weakened market sentiment.

"The central government purposefully allowed a large number of companies with hundreds of millions of shares to debut each day in the leadup to the handover to curb speculation," said an analyst with a major Chinese brokerage.
"The markets are suffering from indigestion with current liquidity unable to quickly absorb the new shares," he said.
"The market lacked capital with foreign investors having little interest in buying," said an analyst with China Guotai Securities Co in Shanghai.
Brokers said China's moves to push domestic investors out of the B share market also hurt sentiment following a meeting held on Friday about the illegal practice.
Bengang Steel Plates Co Ltd, making its debut in Shenzhen, became the year's first stock to close its first day with losses, helping dampen sentiment, they said.
"Bengang fell below the offer price because no one wanted to buy shares in China's lumbering steel sector," said Peter Ho, an analyst at PBI Securities.
"The fact that a share ended its debut at a loss indicates a very bearish mood," Ho said.
The steel issue ended at HK$2.35, against the offer price of HK$2.38, after falling to a low of HK$1.90. Turnover in the stock reached HK$234 million.
Shanghai's A share index ended down 14.993 points or 1.31 percent to 1,160.244 points and its Shenzhen counterpart rose 3.92 points or 1.04 percent to 382.27 points.
The two exchanges each postponed the listing of an A share firm on Tuesday, citing "preparations not ready for the listing" as the excuse of the rare delay, brokers said.

"Investors speculated the move might mean the central government would slow down new share issues," an A share trader said. "This helped the A share markets to a technical rebound in the afternoon, reversing the early losses."
Analysts said they expected the indices to fall another five to 10 percent in the short term if there was no major positive news to support the markets.
On Shanghai's B share market, Shanghai Tyre and Rubber Co was the biggest loser, plunging $0.042 or 9.33 percent to $0.408.
Bengang's performance pulled another new B counter down in Shenzhen, with Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd shedding HK$0.37 to HK$6.42 on volume of 1.4 million shares.
